Month in brief

June 2026 Entra briefing: SSPR registration becomes mandatory in September, partner support assignments close in August, and Excel 2021 has a July authentication deadline

June was dominated by Learn maintenance—5,217 updates versus 32 new items. Representative edits covered native-authentication tutorials, combined-registration troubleshooting, licensing, and lab instructions, so a new page should not be read as a feature launch. The most consequential administrator-facing exceptions were the upcoming SSPR verification change, retirement of new Partner Tier1 and Tier2 Support assignments, the Excel 2021 client deadline, Internet Access web-category changes, and a planned Agent ID service-plan rollout. The supplied record contains no general-availability announcement. Microsoft Entra PIM role-activation extensions are explicitly described as preview, while the new Workload ID assignment-restriction and Lifecycle Workflows execution-limit pages provide guidance without stating availability.

  • Entra ID · Authentication
    SSPR will require explicitly registered authentication methods — 7 September 2026

    This is a change in password-reset verification behavior, not a new SSPR feature announcement. Users will need explicitly registered authentication methods; directory-sourced contact information will no longer be sufficient unless it has been registered. A registration campaign begins on 6 August.

  • Entra ID · Governance
    New Partner Tier1 and Tier2 Support assignments will be blocked — 3 August 2026

    Microsoft Entra is retiring these partner support roles for new assignments. Existing assignments remain valid, and tenants that do not use the roles are unaffected. Scripts that create new assignments should be updated to use alternatives such as User Administrator.

  • Entra ID · Authentication
    Excel 2021 Power Query requires an authentication update — 24 July 2026

    Excel 2021 version 21.08 or earlier must be updated to build 16.0.14334.20754 or later, or upgraded to a newer version, to avoid losing Organizational Account authentication for Power Query. Microsoft 365 and newer Excel versions are unaffected. This is a client requirement, not an Entra service launch.

  • Internet Access · Conditional Access
    Internet Access web categorization changes affect filtering inputs

    The Message Center notice announced a mid-June update that adds an AI Agents category and refines existing categories. Some sites may be reclassified, which can change the results of category-based filtering policies. The notice says no action is required but advises reviewing and adjusting policies if intended access is affected.

  • Security Copilot · Conditional Access
    Agent ID service plans are scheduled for an automatic July rollout

    Microsoft is adding Conditional Access for Agents and ID Protection for Agents to Microsoft Agent 365 and Microsoft 365 E7, with rollout starting in July 2026. The notice specifies automatic enablement and no policy changes or immediate action; it recommends reviewing licensing. This is a planned service-plan rollout, not evidence of a June general-availability feature launch.

For Entra administrators

Prepare users through the SSPR registration campaign beginning 6 August for the 7 September verification change. Inventory Excel 2021 installations at version 21.08 or earlier and update them to build 16.0.14334.20754 or later, or upgrade; Microsoft 365 and newer Excel versions are unaffected. If automation assigns Partner Tier1 or Tier2 Support, change it to an alternative such as User Administrator before 3 August; existing assignments remain valid. For Internet Access, review filtering policies if reclassified sites change intended access—the notice says no action is required. Agent ID service plans are expected to enable automatically, with no policy changes or immediate action, although a license review is recommended. A separate Authenticator notice describes automatic warning-then-­

The export.csv file contains all changes that are about to be exported. Each row corresponds to a change for an object in the connector space and the object is identified by the DN attribute. The DN attribute is a unique identifier assigned to an object in the connector space. When you have many rows/changes in the export.csv to analyze, it may be difficult for you to figure out which objects the changes are for based on the DN attribute alone. To simplify the process of analyzing the changes, use the `csanalyzer.ps1` PowerShell script. The script retrieves common identifiers (for example, displayName, userPrincipalName) of the objects. userimpact: Low

Updated

Microsoft Entra Agent ID requires every [agent identity](/entra/agent-id/agent-identities) and [agent identity blueprint](/entra/agent-id/agent-blueprint) to have at least one sponsor. A sponsor is a human user, or supported group, that holds business accountability for the agent's lifecycle, such as deciding when the agent is no longer needed, approving extensions when access expires, and authorizing suspension during incidents. A sponsor is different from an owner, which designates the human users responsible for technical operations and incident response.

Microsoft Entra Agent ID introduced two identity types: [agent identities](/entra/agent-id/agent-identities) and [agent identity blueprint principals](/entra/agent-id/agent-blueprint). These identity objects derive from service principals, and so carry the same requirements and best practices for ownership, lifecycle management, and cleanup as any service principal. Blueprint principals are the provisioning surface from which agent identities are created and can hold grants that propagate to child agents. This article is for use by the delivery expert that plans on delivering the Microsoft Entra Suite Workshop to customers. It aims to provide delivery experts with a comprehensive overview of the tasks that is required to successfully deliver the Microsoft Entra Suite Workshop to customers. Microsoft Entra External ID pricing is based on monthly active users (MAU), which is the count of unique users with authentication activity within a calendar month. 18 June 2026

Authentication Methods Customers

Updated

With Microsoft Entra External ID, you can create secure, customized sign-in experiences for your consumer- and business customer-facing apps. In an external tenant, there are several ways for users to sign up for your app. They can create an account using their email and either a password or a one-time passcode. Or, if you enable sign-in with Facebook, Google, Apple, a Microsoft Entra ID tenant, or a custom OIDC or SAML/WS-Fed identity provider (IdP), users can sign in using their credentials in the external identity provider. A user object is created for them in your directory with the identity information collected during sign-up.

18 June 2026

Custom Extensions

Updated

Microsoft Entra External ID user flows are designed for flexibility. Within a sign-up and sign-in user flow, there are built-in authentication events. You can also add custom authentication extensions at specific points within the authentication flow. A custom authentication extension is essentially an event listener that, when activated, makes an HTTP call to a REST API endpoint where you define a workflow action. For example, you could add an [attribute collection](#attribute-collection-start-and-submit-events) workflow to validate the attributes a user enters during sign-up, or you could use a [custom claims provider](#token-issuance-start-event) to add external user data to the token before the token is issued.
